_note: OnBuy settings for the image-based wall-art catalogue. AS OF 27 OCT THE FORMAT IS NO LONGER GUESSED: the seller downloaded the real OnCommerce Product Create Template and it is committed at onbuy/OnCommerce_Product_Create_Template.xlsx, with its 83 columns, its required flags and its whole category list extracted to onbuy/template_spec.json. Every column name below is copied from that workbook's Template tab. build_onbuy.py still writes the row data to rows.jsonl as well as to CSV, which is now what feeds build_onbuy_feed.py.
_bucket_note: The largest rendered pool - 480,367 panels - so 10,000 listings drawn from it carry the widest spread of subjects. Three frame colours, and no store_price_adjust, so prices match ebay_plan.json's base. lunar-kms was avoided because the seller was mid-upload with it on eBay and because it carries only the black frame.
_brand_note: NOT 'Unbranded', which is what the eBay files use. OnBuy runs a CATALOGUE: a new product needs the real manufacturer brand, and the barcode exemption is granted on a UK or EU trademark FOR THAT BRAND. 'Unbranded' can be neither trademarked nor exempted. Walryvo is the seller's own brand, held by NORYMUS LIMITED, and is the only name here that can carry the exemption. SELLER DECISION - see README_ONBUY.md.
category_path: Home & Garden > Furniture, Furnishings & Decor > Artwork > Artwork Prints
_category_note: RESOLVED 27 Oct from the template's own Categories tab. 9376 is 'Artwork > Artwork Prints'; the alternatives in that branch are 5611 Posters, 13702 Paintings, 17967 Wall Decorations and 13172 Wall Murals. Artwork Prints is right: these are framed prints, not posters, not paintings and not murals. The Explanation tab says a feed may give its own category or an Amazon/eBay equivalent, but that 'feeds that use OnBuy category IDs/names will be prioritised' - so the full OnBuy PATH is submitted, which is what all four worked examples in the template do. category_submit can be set to 'id' to send 9376 instead.
_unframed_note: NO UNFRAMED VARIANT, and this is the one place the OnBuy file deliberately differs from the eBay one. On eBay the unframed row carries no picture and eBay falls back to the listing's main image - the black frame - which the seller approved for their own account. That does not transfer: a marketplace that shows a picture per variant would be showing a framed photograph for a product with no frame, which is the exact misrepresentation web/catalogue/product.py was restructured to prevent. No unframed photograph exists in this bucket and none can be made: the stored R2 token cannot write to luxvia-art, and the raw panel at <prefix>/gen/<SKU>.jpg is NOT a substitute - it is one image per design rather than one per colourway, and it still carries the uncropped bottom strip where FLUX scrawls a fake signature. So OnBuy launches framed-only, nine variants, every one with its own photograph. Add unframed when a rendered unframed photo exists in this bucket, not before.
_price_note: ONBUY IS GBP 5 UNDER EBAY ON EVERY FRAMED SIZE, and that is the seller's instruction of 27 Oct, not a derived number: eBay's framed 24.99/29.99/34.99 becomes 19.99/24.99/29.99 here. Deliberately different from the eBay and website prices rather than an accident - one design now costs less on OnBuy than on eBay, which is the seller's call on a marketplace they are entering cold. These prices are read ONLY by build_onbuy.py; ebay_plan.json and web/business.config.json are untouched, so changing them here moves nothing on eBay and nothing on walryvo.com.
_weight_note: weight_kg is an ESTIMATE for a packaged framed print and is the one number in this file that was not measured. OnBuy prices delivery off it, so an estimate that is too low is paid for on every order. Weigh one of each size and correct these three numbers before a real upload.
_colourway_note: A design exists in four palettes. eBay lists all four, which is right for a 1.9M catalogue. For a FIRST 10,000 on a new marketplace, one colourway per design means 10,000 distinct designs instead of 2,500 designs four times over - the widest mix for the same row count, and the lowest near-duplicate reading. The other three colourways are untouched and available for later batches. Which colourway is picked is decided by a hash, so it is spread across all four and a rebuild reproduces it.
_dup_note: The same threshold as dup_audit.py, on the same 256-bit gradient hash of the CROPPED ARTWORK, so the number is comparable with every audit before it. luxvia-art is the one bucket with no drop list - the near-duplicate audit was never run on it - so this selection is deduplicated against itself here.

columns._note: CANONICAL FIELD -> COLUMN NAME, copied from the Template tab of the real workbook. The CSV is written with these headers in the template's own column order, which onbuy/template_spec.json holds in full.

_variant_axis_note: Variant_One_Name=Colour (the FRAME colour) and Variant_Two_Name=Size. The template's allowed names are Colour, Length, Material, Pack Quantity, Size, Style, Width, and it warns that a name outside that list is remapped or the products are created as SINGLE products - which would silently turn 10,000 listings into 90,000 unrelated ones. Only two axes exist, which is exactly what we need and no more. The separate 'Colour' FEATURE column is the normalised basic colour, as the worked t-shirt example shows Variant_Two_Value 'Cobalt Blue' against Colour 'Blue'; oak is a wood rather than a colour, so it normalises to Brown.
_rows_note: 50,000 rows a file, not 100,000: a file that has to be read and approved by a person at OnBuy should open in a spreadsheet. Sharding splits on whole listings, so a product row and its nine variants are never in different files.
_unframed_price_note: unframed_when_available is GBP 2 under eBay's print prices - the seller's instruction of 27 Oct, 8.99/12.99/18.99 becoming 6.99/10.99/16.99. IT IS NOT USED BY ANYTHING YET, and the field name says so. The OnBuy file is framed only because no unframed photograph exists in this bucket and none can be made from here - see _unframed_note - so there is no row for this price to go on. It is recorded rather than discarded so that whoever adds the unframed variant does not have to ask again. build_onbuy.py asserts it stays unused while frames carry no unframed entry.
_margin_note: At OnBuy's 15% commission on the delivered total, the new framed prices net 16.99 / 21.24 / 25.49 for A4 / A3 / A2, against 21.24 / 25.49 / 29.74 before the reduction. Nobody here knows the print-and-frame cost, so whether 16.99 on an A4 still clears is the seller's number to check, not an assumption this file should make.
_barcode_note: THE TEMPLATE SETTLES THIS AND IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKED. 'EAN / UPC' is marked REQUIRED on the Explanation tab, and every worked variant example carries its OWN distinct EAN - the sofa's four colours are four barcodes, the t-shirt's size/colour grid one each. So it is not 10,000 barcodes for 10,000 designs, it is ONE PER VARIANT: 90,000 for this file. Note the PARENT rows carry no EAN at all, so whatever is agreed applies to the variant rows only. Buying 90,000 GTINs is not a proposition; the barcode exemption in README_ONBUY.md section 1 is the only route and it is now the single thing standing between this file and an upload.
_rrp_note: RRP IS THE EBAY PRICE, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS HONEST. The template says 'If the RRP is populated, OnBuy will display any savings between the RRP and the seller's price.' On 26 Oct the seller asked for a doubled compare-at price on the website and that was declined, because a reference price the product was never sold at is the clearest misrepresentation there is and Google's sale-price annotation requires real price history. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE CASE. The identical product, same SKU, same photograph, genuinely sells at 24.99/29.99/34.99 on eBay today. Quoting that as the RRP against OnBuy's 19.99/24.99/29.99 shows a saving that is real and checkable, which is exactly what an RRP field is for. If the eBay prices ever move, these move with them - they are read from ebay_plan.json at build time rather than copied here, so they cannot drift.
_max_title_note: The template allows 150 and recommends 50. listing_text.title() builds to eBay's 80-character limit, so there is room to append the variant - '... - Black Frame, A4' - which is what the worked t-shirt example does.
